Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

Apply explicit corrections to the final stated intent. Preserve meaningful filler-like words and unfinished thoughts. Apply clearly spoken punctuation and list cues. Keep the supplied language.", "input": "so on tuesday i tested the log-file cleanup utility against the archive from the north service desk and the main action is forwarding the scan report to mara before the afternoon review the utility found three folders with dated log files and marked the oldest folder for cleanup but it did not delete anything because the retention setting was still active i checked the report on the staging laptop and the file names matched the list from the desk the report also showed that one folder had a blank date field so the utility left that folder out of its age calculation i asked dev to look at the blank field and he said the export came from the older dashboard version for now the cleanup job is set to run only on the test archive and the live archive stays untouched mara needs the report before the review so she can compare the scan details with the desk inventory if the blank date field is still there after the dashboard export is refreshed we can include it in the next test i saved the scan output beside the weekly notes and put the test time in the handoff log there is no deletion record from this run and the forwarding step is waiting for the report attachment", "output": "So on Tuesday, I tested the log-file cleanup utility against the archive from the north service desk, and the main action is forwarding the scan report to Mara before the afternoon review. The utility found three folders with dated log files and marked the oldest folder for cleanup, but it did not delete anything because the retention setting was still active. I checked the report on the staging laptop, and the file names matched the list from the desk. The report also showed that one folder had a blank date field, so the utility left that folder out of its age calculation. I asked Dev to look at the blank field, and he said the export came from the older dashboard version. For now, the cleanup job is set to run only on the test archive, and the live archive stays untouched. Mara needs the report before the review so she can compare the scan details with the desk inventory. If the blank date field is still there after the dashboard export is refreshed, we can include it in the next test. I saved the scan output beside the weekly notes and put the test time in the handoff log. There is no deletion record from this run, and the forwarding step is waiting for the report attachment."}]
